item.title: Postdoctoral Researcher in Process Mining (m/f/x)
item.description:
Institution: Faculty of Mathematics, Informatics and Statistics

Remuneration: TV-L

Application deadline: 2025-05-14T21:59:00+00:00

Job Details:

About us:

<p>With our research activities, we drive forward concepts for Data Mining, Process Mining, Data Science, Machine Learning in the area of Artificial Intelligence. Our goal is to enhance methods for the analysis of large and complex datasets from various fields including engineering, economics, humanities, life sciences, etc. Both our fundamental and applied research activities inspire and support each other. Members of our group strengthen their scientific qualification and extend their research and teaching profiles. We operate in the heart of the Munich Center for Machine Learning (MCML).</p>

Your qualifications:

<ul> <li>Excellent or upcoming doctoral degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Data Science, or related research field.</li> <li>Experience in one or more areas as mentioned in the above.</li> <li>Publications in leading specialized journals or conferences in the area of Process Mining, Data Mining, Machine Learning, or related fields.</li> <li>Experience in supervising student research projects.</li> <li>Good communication skills, fluent in English, and ideally knowledgeable in German.</li> </ul>

Benefits:

<p>You will work at LMU Munich in the ecosystem of one of Germany and Europe's leading AI research regions, with access to an excellent network of researchers. With the national AI competence center, Munich Center for Machine Learning, the Munich region has a unique network of top researchers nationwide. Your workplace is centrally located at the English Garden in Munich and is easily accessible by public transportation. The salary is based on the <a href="https://www.tdl-online.de/fileadmin/downloads/TV-L/TV-L_Anlagen/TV-L_Anlage_B_g%C3%BCltig_ab_01.02.2025.pdf">German TV-L scale</a>, up to remuneration group TV-L E14, depending on the fulfillment of requirements. The position is limited to three years, with the possibility of extension. We welcome applications from women.</p>

Contact: <p>To apply, please send the following documents in a single PDF file (max 5 MB) to Prof. Dr. Thomas Seidl at <a href="mailto:seidl.office@dbs.ifi.lmu.de">seidl.office@dbs.ifi.lmu.de</a> <strong>by May 12th, 2025</strong>:</p> <ul> <li>Certificate of your doctoral degree or proof of registration for the doctoral exam.</li> <li>Academic CV with Google Scholar link.</li> <li>Outline for a research project (one to two pages).</li> <li>Names and contact information of two references.</li> </ul>

item.title: PhD position in the Institute of Clinical Neuroimmunology (m/f/x)
item.description:
Institution: Faculty of Medicine

Remuneration: TV-L E13

Application deadline: 2025-05-30T21:59:00+00:00

Job Details:

About us:

<p>The <a href="https://www.neuroimmunology-munich.de/our-labs/meinl-lab/3dc4a633666a8413">Institute of Clinical Neuroimmunology</a> is devoted to research into the mechanisms and treatment of multiple sclerosis (MS) and related diseases. Our institute combines reseach at the biomedical center (BMC) with taking care for patients at the Klinikum Großhadern. This infrastructure is ideally suited for joining basic research with clinically relevant issues.</p> <p>Background and project: Inflammatory diseases of the CNS comprise a spectrum of disorders amongst which MS is the most frequent one. These diseases are due to misguided autoreactive immune cells that attack the own nervous system and induce chronic inflammation. We aim to (1) explore the autoimmunity against known target antigens and identify novel targets of autoimmune responses to stratify patients, (2) recognize mechanisms of actions of immunomodulatory drugs applied to patients with MS and related disorders. This specific project aims at understanding the role of B cells and plasma cells in neuroinflammation and will be performed in the BMC in the lab of Prof. Dr. Edgar Meinl.</p>

Your qualifications:

<ul> <li>MSc or equivalent degree in Biology, Immunology, Biochemistry or a related discipline. Alternative: MD with a strong interest in basic research</li> <li>Enthusiasm for joining basic research with clinically relevant issues</li> <li>Experience with FACS, immune cell culture, molecular biology techniques and bioinformatics is advantageous</li> <li>Strong communication skills and fluency in English (spoken and written).</li> </ul>

Benefits:

<ul> <li>Fully funded PhD positions with competitive salaries according to<a href="https://www.tdl-online.de/fileadmin/downloads/TV-L/TV-L_Anlagen/TV-L_Anlage_B_g%C3%BCltig_ab_01.02.2025.pdf"> TV-L scale</a>.</li> <li>Integration into the LMU Graduate Program, providing structured career development and training.</li> <li>Access to cutting-edge core facilities (on-site) in genomics, proteomics, imaging, and computational biology.</li> <li>Close supervision and mentorship to support scientific and career development.</li> <li>Financial support for conference participation and workshops.</li> <li>A stimulating and interdisciplinary<a href="https://www.med.lmu.de/bmc/en/about-us/campus-life/"> research environment at the BMC</a>, LMU Munich, part of the HighTech Campus, home to leading research institutes and fostering collaboration and access to top-tier facilities.</li> <li>Work in a highly international, collaborative, and interdisciplinary research setting.</li> <li>Many opportunities to help shape our <a href="https://www.med.lmu.de/bmc/en/about-us/our-values/">BMC initiatives</a> (e.g. BMC Green Lab, Public Outreach and BMC working group diversity and inclusion)</li> <li>Compatibility of family and science (e.g. parent room and kindergarten on campus, school holiday and emergency child care)</li> <li>Numerous<a href="https://www.med.lmu.de/bmc/en/jobs-career/working-here/"> LMU employee benefits</a>, e.g. discounted fitness and cultural offers, job public transport ticket, Jobbike as well as several canteens and excellent cafés on campus</li> <li>Annual special payment, 30 days of vacation and additional pension scheme</li> </ul> <p>We welcome applications from all backgrounds. The promotion of diversity is an important strategic goal at BMC. This is reflected in the<a href="https://www.med.lmu.de/bmc/en/about-us/our-values/bmc-code-of-conduct/"> BMC Code of Conduct</a>, which actively promotes diversity and equal opportunities.</p> <p>Destination Germany</p> <p>Do you have questions about visa requirements or degree recognition? Are you looking for housing, childcare, or trying to decide on the best health insurance? The "<a href="https://www.research-in-bavaria.de/moving-to-germany/">Research in Bavaria</a>" website provides help in these practical matters.</p>

Contact: <p>Interested candidates should submit a single PDF file (max. 5 MB) containing:</p> <ul> <li>Curriculum Vitae (PDF file, max. two pages, written in English).</li> <li>Short description of research projects carried out during your studies (e.g., MSc thesis). Please describe the rationale and goals of the research, and highlight your contributions to the results (approx. 300 words).</li> <li>Description of your general research interests (approx. 200 words).</li> <li>What do you find interesting about our research group and topics? (approx. 200 words).</li> <li>Transcript (record of study) and degree certificate for all completed degrees. Please also include any supplementary information provided by the university, if available.</li> <li>Temporary/provisional transcripts for any ongoing degree programs.</li> <li>Contact details for at least two referees, including at least one direct supervisor who has worked with you for at least six months.</li> </ul> <p>Important dates<br /> <strong>Application deadline: 30/05/2025</strong><br /> Start date: Flexible, between July and September 2025<br /> Contact & Submission: Please send applications to <a href="mailto:edgar.meinl@med.uni-muenchen.de">edgar.meinl@med.uni-muenchen.de</a> with the subject “Application for PhD Position”.<br /> <a href="https://www.neuroimmunology-munich.de/our-labs/meinl-lab/3dc4a633666a8413">Website</a></p>

item.title: Doctoral Researcher in Assyriology at the ERC Project: “Rewriting the End of Cuneiform Civilization” (m/f/x)
item.description:
Institution: Faculty for the Study of Culture

Remuneration: TV-L E13

Application deadline: 2025-06-30T21:59:00+00:00

Job Details:

About us:

<p>The <a href="https://www.assyriologie.uni-muenchen.de/index.html">Institute for Assyriology and Hittitology</a> is a leading center for cutting-edge research in Digital Assyriology, with a strong focus on the digital preservation and analysis of cuneiform sources.</p> <p>The ERC-funded project “Rewriting the End of Cuneiform Civilization” (RECC) aims to revolutionize our understanding of the final centuries of cuneiform culture through cutting-edge digital humanities and machine learning techniques. The project will develop tools for paleographic analysis, automatic dating of cuneiform tablets, and the study of scribal practices in Hellenistic and Parthian Babylonia.</p>

Your qualifications:

<ul> <li>Master’s degree in <strong>Assyriology</strong> (or equivalent) with top grades.</li> <li>Experience reading <strong>cuneiform tablets</strong>.</li> <li>Familiarity with digital tools (e.g., eBL platform, ATF transliteration).</li> <li>Fluency in English; German is a plus.</li> </ul>

Benefits:

<ul> <li>The opportunity to be part of a dynamic, internationally connected team working at the forefront of Digital Assyriology.</li> <li>Career development through the LMU qualification program.</li> <li>A stimulating working environment at one of Germany’s top-ranked universities. Our institute is located in the heart of the vibrant and internationally diverse city of Munich with excellent public transportation links.</li> <li>Organizational assistance from the LMU Gateway service for relocation to Munich.</li> <li>Collaboration with Assyriologists, ML experts, and international partners.</li> <li>Flexible working hours.</li> </ul>

Contact: <p>If you have any questions, please contact Prof. Dr. Enrique Jiménez: <a href="mailto:enrique.jimenez@lmu.de" title="E-Mail senden an: enrique.jimenez@lmu.de">enrique.jimenez@lmu.de</a></p> <p>Submit your <strong>CV, academic transcripts, writing sample</strong> (e.g. MA thesis), and <strong>motivation letter (one to two pages)</strong> as a single PDF to: <a href="mailto:sekretariat.jimenez@assyr.fak12.uni-muenchen.de">sekretariat.jimenez@assyr.fak12.uni-muenchen.de</a></p> <p>Subject: <strong>_Application for PhD1 (RECC Project)</strong>_</p>

Job Details:

About us:

<p>The Department of Chemistry is an internationally recognized research institution with an interdisciplinary research environment in the fields of synthetic chemistry, organometallic chemistry, chemical biology, catalysis and supramolecular chemistry. The Chair of Organic and Biological Chemistry works at the interface between chemistry and biochemistry and is one of 14 chairs in the faculty. It is internationally visible in research and was newly filled on 01.01.2024. For more information about our research and teaching activities, please visit our <a href="https://www.rentmeister-group.com/">website</a>.</p>

Your qualifications:

<ul> <li>PhD in Chemistry or Biochemistry</li> <li>Experience in synthetic organic chemistry and operation of HPLC and LC-MS</li> <li>Willingness to become the safety officer for the isotope lab (including participation at   the required courses)</li> <li>English (level B2 or higher)</li> <li>Ability for and willingness to work in a multidisciplinary team</li> <li>Willingness to learn German and teach in German</li> </ul> <p><strong>Desirable skills</strong></p> <ul> <li>Preference will be given to candidates with experience in one or more of the following: <ul> <li>Nucleotide chemistry</li> <li>Quantitative LC-MS analysis of nucleosides</li> <li>Radioactive labeling of nucleic acids [32P]</li> <li>German</li> </ul> </li> </ul>

Benefits:

<ul> <li>The position is initially designed for five years. If all formal requirements are met, the position can be linked to a civil-servant status (“akademischer Rat, verbeamtet”) and paid according to A13 pay scale.</li> <li>Opportunity to engage in well-funded, innovative research projects</li> <li>Work alongside a diverse team of scientists, including chemists, biologists, and bioinformaticians, fostering a collaborative and vibrant research environment</li> <li>State-of-art chemistry and biochemistry labs.</li> </ul>

Contact: <p>If you have any questions, please contact: Prof. Andrea Rentmeister  at <a href="tel:4989218073470">+49 89 2180  73470</a> or Dr. Martin Sumser at <a href="tel:4989218077765">+49 89 2180 77765</a></p> <p>Applications, including a cover letter, curriculum vitae, qualifying documentation (final academic records, list of publications, evidence of external funding, teaching experience, prizes), and the names and contact information of up to three references should be submitted by email (all documents together in one PDF) <strong>by 01.06.2025</strong> to Dr. Martin Sumser (<a href="mailto:martin.sumser@lmu.de">martin.sumser@lmu.de</a>).</p>

item.title: Research Associate (Post-doctoral Researcher) in Syriac Studies (m/f/x)
item.description:
Institution: Faculty for the Study of Culture

Remuneration: TV-L E13

Application deadline: 2025-05-15T21:59:00+00:00

Job Details:

About us:

<p>The ERC-funded project “The Challenge of Islam and the Transformation of Eastern Christian Normative Regimes, ca. 630-1100” (NOMOS), directed by Prof. Dr. Zachary Chitwood and housed at the Chair for Byzantine Studies within the Institute for Byzantine Studies, Byzantine Art History and Modern Greek Studies at the Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich, is hiring three post-doctoral researchers for a period of four years each.</p> <p>In the crucial half-millennium between the death of the Prophet Muhammad and the First Crusade, an absolutely essential part in the origins of Christian-Muslim relations has been overlooked, namely how the normative regimes of Eastern Christians – including those of Byzantium, the Islamicate world and the space in between – grappled with the rise of Islam. Exploring this history has important implications for our understanding of the development of Christian-Muslim relations in the premodern period, the genesis of Eastern Christian legal regimes and the earlier precedents which Eastern Mediterranean states after the year 1100 might have drawn on in dealing with Islam.</p>

Your qualifications:

<ul> <li>You have completed a PhD.</li> <li>You have excellent knowledge of Syriac.</li> <li>You have a good command of either English or German.</li> <li>You have experience with Digital Humanities, or the willingness to acquire some.</li> <li>You have experience with legal history, or the willingness to acquire some.</li> </ul>

Benefits:

<ul> <li>Your workplace will be in the center of Munich with easy accessibility by public transportation</li> <li>You will be paid according to the <a href="https://oeffentlicher-dienst.info/c/t/rechner/tv-l/allg?id=tv-l-2025&matrix=1"><strong>TV-L E13</strong></a> salary scheme.</li> <li>University support for families and children: for more  information on the Family Service of LMU click <a href="https://www.lmu.de/en/about-lmu/working-at-lmu/additional-services/diversity/being-family-friendly/family-service/index.html"><strong>here</strong></a>.</li> <li>Access to discounted health, mobility and promotional offers as a university employee: for more information click <a href="https://www.lmu.de/en/about-lmu/working-at-lmu/additional-services/corporate-benefits/">here</a>.</li> </ul> <p>LMU Munich is an equal opportunity employer and committed to enhancing the diversity of its faculty.</p>

Contact: <p>Please send your application (including cover letter, CV, list of publications, copies of certificates), a writing sample (e.g., a chapter of your dissertation or a publication) <strong>by 15 May 2025 at the latest</strong> as a single PDF:  <a href="mailto:byzantinistik@lrz.uni-muenchen.de">byzantinistik@lrz.uni-muenchen.de</a>. Please indicate in the subject line of the e-mail: <em>“NOMOS application Syriac”</em>.</p> <p>Shortlisted applicants will be invited to an (online) interview.</p> <p>Your tenure in the position should begin no later than 1 October 2025.</p> <p>If you have any questions, please contact Prof. Dr. Zachary Chitwood (<a href="mailto:Zachary.Chitwood@lmu.de">Zachary.Chitwood@lmu.de</a>).</p>

item.title: Computational Postdoctoral positions in Gene Regulation and Chromatin Metabolism (m/f/x)
item.description:
Institution: Faculty of Medicine

Remuneration: TV-L

Application deadline: 2025-05-31T21:59:00+00:00

Job Details:

About us:

<p>The Russo lab is a new research group in the Physiological Chemistry Department and is funded, among others, by an Emmy Noether (DFG) grant. We are looking for a highly motivated Computational Postdoctoral Fellow to help establish this research group from the ground up, shaping an innovative and dynamic lab environment together.</p> <p>The Russo lab investigates how nuclear acyl-CoA metabolism influences chromatin remodelling, transcriptional regulation, and cellular plasticity. Although acyl-CoA-producing enzymes have been extensively studied in the mitochondrial compartment for decades, emerging evidence suggests they are also present and functional in the nucleus, where they play a key role in gene regulation.</p> <p>By employing omics-based approaches, metabolite tracing, proximity-labeling, and advanced imaging techniques,</p> <p>this project offers a unique opportunity to:</p> <ul> <li>Explore how nuclear metabolic enzymes functionally regulate gene expression and chromatin modifications during cellular responses to external stimuli.</li> <li>Identify novel protein-protein interactions between these nuclear metabolic enzymes and chromatin factors.</li> <li>Study the biochemical and structural properties of these metabolic enzymes in the nuclear context.</li> </ul>

Your qualifications:

<ul> <li>PhD in Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Genomics, or a related discipline.</li> <li>Experience in the analysis of functional genomics and proteomics data.</li> <li>Familiarity with chromatin and transcriptional regulation.</li> <li>Ability to work independently and collaboratively in an interdisciplinary setting.</li> <li>Strong scientific writing and communication skills.</li> </ul>

Benefits:

<ul> <li>Fully funded Postdoc position with competitive salaries according to TV-L scale.</li> <li>Access to professional development programs at LMU, including workshops, training, and career support for postdoctoral researchers.</li> <li>Access to cutting-edge core facilities in genomics, proteomics, imaging, and computational biology on-site.</li> <li>Close supervision and mentorship to support scientific and career development.</li> <li>Financial support for conference participation and workshops.</li> <li>A stimulating and interdisciplinary<a href="https://www.med.lmu.de/bmc/en/about-us/campus-life/"> research environment at the BMC</a>, LMU Munich, part of the HighTech Campus, home to leading research institutes and fostering collaboration and access to top-tier facilities.</li> <li>Work in a highly international, collaborative, and interdisciplinary research setting.</li> <li>Many opportunities to help shape our<a href="https://www.med.lmu.de/bmc/en/about-us/our-values/"> BMC initiatives</a> (e.g. BMC Green Lab, Public Outreach, BMC Diversity and BMC Postdoc)</li> <li>Compatibility of family and science (e.g. parent room and kindergarten on campus, school holiday and emergency child care)</li> <li>Numerous<a href="https://www.med.lmu.de/bmc/en/jobs-career/working-here/"> LMU employee benefits</a>, e.g. discounted fitness and cultural offers, job public transport ticket, Jobbike as well as several canteens and excellent cafés on campus</li> <li>Annual special payment, 30 days of vacation and additional pension scheme</li> </ul> <p>We welcome applications from all backgrounds. The promotion of diversity is an important strategic goal at BMC. This is reflected in the <a href="https://www.med.lmu.de/bmc/en/about-us/our-values/bmc-code-of-conduct/">BMC Code of Conduct</a>, which actively promotes diversity and equal opportunities.</p> <p><strong>Destination Germany</strong></p> <p>Do you have questions about visa requirements or degree recognition? Are you looking for housing, childcare, or trying to decide on the best health insurance? The "<a href="https://www.research-in-bavaria.de/moving-to-germany/">Research in Bavaria</a>" website provides help in these practical matters.</p>

Contact: <p><strong>Application Process</strong><br /> Interested candidates should submit a single PDF file (max. 5 MB) containing:</p> <ul> <li> <strong>Curriculum Vitae</strong> (PDF file, max. 2 pages, written in English).</li> <li> <strong>Short description of research projects</strong> carried out during your studies (e.g., PhD thesis). Please describe the rationale and goals of the research, and highlight your contributions to the results (approx. 300 words).</li> <li> <strong>Description of your general research interests</strong> (approx. 200 words).</li> <li> <strong>What do you find interesting about our research group and topics?</strong> (approx. 200 words).</li> <li> <strong>Transcript (record of study) and degree certificate</strong> for all completed degrees. Please also include any supplementary information provided by the university, if available.</li> <li> <strong>Temporary/provisional transcripts</strong> for any ongoing degree programs.</li> <li>Contact details for at least two referees, including at least one direct supervisor who has worked with you for at least six months.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Important dates</strong><br /> <strong>Application deadline</strong>: 31/05/2025<br /> <strong>Start date</strong>: Flexible, between July and September 2025<br /> Contact & Submission: Please send applications to <a href="mailto:marta.russolab@gmail.com">Marta Russo</a> with the subject <strong>“Application for Postdoc Position – BMC_LMU Munich”</strong>.</p> <p>Further websites: <a href="https://www.med.lmu.de/bmc/en/research/research-groups/russo-lab/">Russo Lab page</a></p>

item.title: Doctoral researcher at LAFUGA Proteomics / Gene Center in Großhadern/Martinsried (m/f/x)
item.description:
Institution: Faculty of Chemistry and Pharmacy

Remuneration: TV-L E13

Application deadline: 2025-05-15T21:59:00+00:00

Job Details:

About us:

<p>The <a href="https://www.genzentrum.uni-muenchen.de/research-groups/lafuga/froehlich/index.html">Laboratory for Functional Genome Analysis (LAFUGA)</a> is an integrated technology platform within the <a href="https://www.genzentrum.uni-muenchen.de/index.html">Gene Center</a>, consisting of the three research units Genomics, Proteomics and Model Organisms. With the establishment of efficient and precise techniques for genetic modification of pigs, it is possible to generate customized pig models that mimic human disease mechanisms at the molecular and functional level. Using state-of-the-art quantitative proteomics to analyze samples from transgenic pig models, we are complementing basic pathological findings with high-throughput data for a better understanding of molecular pathology. In addition to new functional insights, we aim to identify disease-specific protein markers and protein target candidates for diagnostic and therapeutic applications. For discovery proteomics our research facility uses state-of-the-art instrumentation including nano-HPLC systems and high-resolution FT mass spectrometers.</p>

Your qualifications:

<ul> <li>An excellent Master’s degree (or equivalent) in veterinary medicine, biology, biochemistry, analytical chemistry or similar.</li> <li>Solid experience in biochemical / molecular biology techniques.</li> <li>Expertise in bioinformatics or R are advantageous.</li> <li>Interest in mass spectrometry-based proteomics.</li> <li>Willingness to contribute effectively to interdisciplinary collaborations.</li> <li>Excellent communication skills in English, proficiency in German is advantageous.</li> </ul>
